blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus had been arrested in the night, questioned, beaten and sentenced. Now they led him outside the city walls to a hill, with two other men who were to be put to death beside him.

verses.text: And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The first words he spoke from the cross were a prayer.

verses.text: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He prayed for the very people who were putting him to death. Even there, he was forgiving.

verses.text: And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also with them derided him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he be Christ, the chosen of God.

verses.text: And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, and offering him vinegar,

verses.text: And saying, If thou be the king of the Jews, save thyself.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And saying,

segments.speaker: soldiers
segments.text: If thou be the king of the Jews, save thyself.

verses.text: And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Save yourself. They said it over and over. The leaders, the soldiers, and then one of the men dying beside him. They could not understand that he was staying on that cross on purpose. He saved others by not saving himself.

verses.text: And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.

segments.text: And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying,

segments.text: If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.

verses.text: But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the other answering rebuked him, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?

verses.text: And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The second man had nothing left to offer. No good works, no time to fix his life. Only a few words.

verses.text: And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said unto Jesus,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.

verses.text: And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Today. Not someday. A dying man asked only to be remembered, and Jesus gave him a promise.

verses.text: And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.

verses.text: And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.

segments.speaker: narrator

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Darkness at noon. The thick curtain in the temple, which hung before the holiest place, tore down the middle.

verses.text: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He did not have his life taken from him like a man who has lost. He gave it into his Father's hands.

verses.text: Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: A Roman soldier, who had seen many men die, watched this one and gave glory to God.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The cross is the hardest place in the whole story, and it is where the love of God is seen most clearly. Jesus forgave the people who hurt him. He welcomed a dying man who had nothing to bring. And he trusted his Father all the way to the end. The story does not stop here. But it is right to stand here a while, and be still, and remember what he did.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Luke 23:33-47; crucifixion tagged violence mild and kept off the page (no wound detail); no blame of 'the Jews' for the death; 'today' given as the text gives it, no doctrine of what paradise is; ends in stillness, pointing on to the resurrection.

cultural.note: Reverent; the dying thief shown with dignity; a deacon board would read it on Good Friday.
